site_ui.lead: Merchant-services and ATM operators show how card fees split among issuing banks, card brands, processors, and ISOs, and how agents turn the processor markup into monthly residual income.
site_ui.summary: All 12 chapters synthesize 192 verbatim YouTube practitioner testimonies, with every quote, metric, and tip carrying timestamped inline attribution to its source video. The chapters run from card processing flow, pricing models, and interchange optimization through dual pricing, surcharging, residual economics, ISO building, high-risk accounts, and ATM unit economics, locations, hardware, and vault cash.

flow: Open with a free cost analysis: divide total interchange by volume to land near 1.7 percent, then subtract interchange from total fees to expose the real markup.
Pull the average ticket and card mix first; tickets under about 15 dollars need per-item fees that cover the 22-cent regulated debit cost.
Verify the SIC or MCC code and the card-present versus card-not-present setup so the merchant is not miscoded into higher rates.
Price from Schedule A costs on interchange plus, charging the cost of the card plus a set margin such as 0.25 or 0.60 percent so Durbin cost drops pass through.
Resolve past-due gateway accounts before they go delinquent, since after 6 months of uncollected fees the balance is debited from the affiliate account.
Collect the residual on the split: at 80/20, 280 dollars of gross profit on a 20,000-dollar-per-month cafe pays the agent 224 dollars every month.
